articles.title: Annual SJAA Awards and Potluck Dinner Report
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) hosted its Annual Awards and Potluck Dinner on February 20, 2016, celebrating significant contributions from numerous members. Awards recognized individuals for their service on the board of directors, leadership in programs like "Intro to the Night Sky," extensive public outreach participation, and involvement in the solar program, alongside holding club elections and fostering social interaction.

articles.title: From Rob Jaworski
articles.summary: The 2015 SJAA Swap Meet was a significant success, attracting many attendees who bought, sold, and socialized, leading to an early wrap-up. The club utilized the event to sell donated astronomy gear, including telescopes and accessories, ultimately raising approximately $2300. The article expresses gratitude for donations and the efforts of volunteers and the amateur astronomy community, while also encouraging continued participation in club activities.

articles.title: A Planetary Quintet is Dancing Across the Skies
articles.summary: Early risers have a unique opportunity to witness a rare alignment of five naked-eye planets—Mercury, Venus, Saturn, Mars, and Jupiter—visible simultaneously in the pre-dawn sky from late January through late February. This celestial spectacle, last seen in 2004-2005, offers sky-watchers specific times and directions for viewing the planets across the horizon, with the Moon also joining the display during this period. The event also serves as a reminder of NASA's extensive exploration of these solar system bodies.

articles.title: First Flower Grown in Space Station's Veggie Facility
articles.summary: Expedition 46 Commander Scott Kelly successfully grew a zinnia flower aboard the International Space Station's Veggie facility in January 2016, marking a significant achievement in space horticulture. This experiment provided scientists with valuable data on plant growth in microgravity and gave astronauts crucial practice in autonomous gardening, essential for future deep space missions. Kelly's independent decision-making in plant care, guided by simplified procedures, proved vital for the successful bloom.

articles.title: Hubble Offers a Dazzling 'Necklace'
articles.summary: The Hubble Space Telescope has captured a stunning image of the recently discovered Necklace Nebula, a planetary nebula located 15,000 light-years away in the constellation Sagitta. This cosmic "necklace" was formed by a pair of closely orbiting stars, where one star engulfed its companion, causing it to spin rapidly and expel gas into a glowing ring dotted with dense knots. The composite image highlights the emissions of hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen.

articles.title: SJAA Member Observation Posts
articles.summary: This document compiles several observation reports from members of the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) from late 2015 to early 2016, detailing their backyard observations despite challenging weather conditions. Members shared experiences viewing various celestial objects, including nebulae, galaxies, multiple open clusters, carbon stars, double stars, planets, and Comet C/2013 US10 Catalina, often using specific equipment and techniques. The reports highlight the satisfaction of opportunistic viewing, discovery, and shared astronomical experiences among the community.

articles.title: Member Contributions and News Updates
articles.summary: This article features contributions from SJAA members, including Anand's account of successful moon observations and iPhone astrophotography. It also details Natti Pierce-Thompson's report on the groundbreaking ceremony for West Valley College's new state-of-the-art planetarium, highlighting its advanced features and educational mission. Finally, Sukhada Palav announces new book additions to the SJAA library from a generous donation, while also informing members about giving away magazine collections due to limited space.

articles.title: Kid Spot Quiz
articles.summary: This document features a 'Kid Spot Quiz' with three astronomy questions, accompanied by a 'Did You Know?' section offering diverse astronomical facts. Topics range from historical discoveries and space missions like New Horizons and Huygens, to properties of celestial bodies such as the Sun and Saturn, and astronomical concepts like star systems and sunspot cycles. Answers to the quiz are provided at the end.

articles.title: From the Board of Directors
articles.summary: The Board of Directors announces a call for volunteers to assist with various SJAA programs. As of January 2016, total membership stands at 358. Upcoming events include a work party on March 19th to prepare for the annual SJAA Swap Meet, which will be held on March 20th starting at 12pm.

articles.title: Board Meeting Excerpts
articles.summary: These board meeting excerpts from November 2015 to January 2016 detail discussions and decisions made by the SJAA board. Key topics included streamlining the 'Fix-It' program, navigating the City of San Jose's reuse bid process for Houge Park facilities, and addressing the need for new volunteers. The board also focused on planning club events like the annual auction (later decided to be replaced by a swap meet), developing a loaner equipment program, establishing the Robert Armstrong scholarship, and approving budgets for publicity and a new printer for Houge Park.

articles.title: SJAA Library and Programs
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) offers a variety of resources and programs for its members and the community, including a library of astronomy books and DVDs. They provide free telescope repair sessions, regular solar observing events, and beginner-friendly programs like Quick STARt and Intro to the Night Sky. Additionally, SJAA has a loaner equipment program, an Astro Imaging Special Interest Group (SIG), and hands-on astro-imaging workshops and field clinics to support various levels of astronomical interest.
